title: Deployed Systems Engineer
description:
At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a small team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools. We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), and Gokul Rajaram. We've 3x'd our ARR this year, and our customers range from your friends in the YC batch to Wabi, Glean, Zoom and many more.

running stateful agent infrastructure inside someone else's cluster is new territory. this role defines what reliable, repeatable on-prem agent deployment looks like, across the customers running us in their own environments.

THE FRONTIER YOU'LL WORK ON

• fleet-managing agent runtimes across air-gapped, regulated, BYOK environments has no playbook. you define one.

• turning hand-managed on-prem deployments into a repeatable product. the difference between 5 self-hosted customers and 50.

• every incident, CVE, and upgrade wave here is unsolved at the ecosystem level. your runbooks lead the industry.

WHAT YOU'LL DO?

• own the on-prem lifecycle: helm charts, upgrades, the weekly release train, rollback paths.

• drive chart convergence: diverged customer forks back onto one supported chart, with guardrails.

• build structured onboarding (replicated or equivalent) so a new customer deploys in days, not weeks.

• debug across the stack: temporal workflows, k8s init ordering, storage backends, auth-refresh pipelines.

• own the security surface: CVE triage, patching, RCAs, bulletins. keep customers running when releases freeze.

• co-own per-customer tool patching with the platform team.

• dogfood Composio on your own deployment and support workflows.

"MUST HAVES"

if you are very good, nothing is a must per-se

• core infra engineering

– you've run software in environments you don't control: on-prem, VPC, air-gapped.

– deep kubernetes and helm: chart authoring, init-job ordering, multi-environment releases.

– you keep systems reliable while the product moves fast.

• fleet judgment

– you think in version skew, upgrade waves, and rollback paths across many instances.

– you separate one customer's bespoke ask from the primitive every install needs.

• ai native

– you have built with the language models.

– you have opinions on agents, MCP, and where they break in real deployments.

• linux - comfortable deep in the stack.

• typist - your RCAs and security notes earn customer trust.

• human - you build trust and admit what you don't know.

OPTIONAL

• temporal, Postgres, cloud secret managers (GCP / AWS).

• replicated or packaged self-hosted delivery (kots, airgap bundles).

• compliance: SOC 2, Vanta-style programs, security questionnaires.

• major open source contributions.

title: Growth and Data Engineer
description:
At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a small team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools.

We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with some incredible angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), Gokul Rajaram. Beginning of this year we 3x our ARR, our customers range from your friends in the YC batch to Wabi, Glean, Zoom and many more.

Our product is used by prosumers (MCP / CLI), developers (SDK), and enterprises. The job of the growth team is to increase usage and revenue across all three products. We accomplish this with a ruthless focus on analytics to inform the products we ship, features we highlight, and leads we hand off to sales. We're looking to hire a talented engineer who is as comfortable in SQL as they are in nextJS - someone who's excited to own the analytics foundations of the company and use it to drive our next phase of growth.




WHAT YOU'LL DO?

 - Own our data foundation. Build and run the data lake and analytics stack that ties together all three products - MCP/CLI, SDK, and enterprise. You'll own Snowflake end to end: building pipelines, modeling clean generated tables, keeping the data trustworthy, and being the person who can answer the questions nobody else can.

 - Turn behavior into decisions. Dig into how people actually use Composio, chase down the trickiest analytics questions, and translate what you find into roadmap calls - what to double down on, what to kill, and what deserves the next bet. This work directly guides where product invests.

 - Build the product-led sales engine. Instrument our funnels and flag PLS signals into Snowflake so consumer and developer usage becomes a clean, agile handoff to sales. Connecting a prosumer's MCP usage or a developer's SDK adoption to the right enterprise conversation is core to how we grow.

 - Ship growth features in the product. You're as comfortable in Next.js as in SQL. You'll build in-product upsells, sharpen onboarding and ship new onboarding flows, and drive in-app actions like booking a sales meeting - without ever making it feel bolted on. The experience stays delightful.

 - Own activation and retention. Run email activation and reactivation campaigns, close funnel gaps, and take these problems from goal to shipped without waiting for a PM to turn them into tickets.

 - Scope ruthlessly. Ship the narrow, signal-generating version today, read the data, then either kill the idea or build it properly.

 - Work across the company. Partner with product, sales, marketing, and engineering to turn distribution ideas into shipped product.
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The data instinct is the part that's hard to teach. Strong engineers can round out the rest quickly, so we weight it accordingly.

 - Data fluency (non-negotiable). You write SQL fluently, are at home living in a warehouse like Snowflake, and can model data, stand up tracking, build dashboards, and reason clearly from messy funnel data. You're genuinely curious about user behavior and driven to answer the hardest questions. This is the heart of the role.

 - Strong engineer. You ship polished frontend and backend systems and context-switch across codebases without losing speed. If your product-engineering chops are still catching up to your data ability, that's fine - we'd rather hire a great data mind who's hungry to round out the full stack than the reverse.

 - Growth taste. You know the difference between a cheap experiment and a sloppy product, and you'd rather ship a narrow signal-generating version today than a perfect unknown next week.

 - AI-native. You build with LLMs and keep up with what's happening in the ecosystem.

 - Owner. You take a goal, decide what to build, ship it, measure whether it worked, and flex across all of the above.

 - Human. You build trust and admit what you don't know.
   


STRONG PREFERENCE FOR

 - Hands-on experience with Snowflake (or a comparable warehouse) in production — modeling, pipelines, and performance

 - Fluency with Next.js and modern full-stack web development

 - Prior growth or product engineering at a startup
   


BONUS POINTS

 - You've built something that got real traction

 - A presence in the AI community through open source, writing, or building in public

 - Interest in owning performance marketing and media mix modeling — measuring and disentangling what's actually driving growth across channels

title: Member Technical Staff - Applied AI Engineer (US Timing)
description:
Member of Technical Staff – Applied AI Engineering

EXPERIENCE:  2–4 years  
TYPE: Full-time          
FOCUS: Applied AI Customer-facing                    
WORK HOURS:  US Timings
LOCATION: Bengaluru



ABOUT THE COMPANY

At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows AI agents to communicate with the tools people use for work, including GitHub, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, and more. We are a small team of engineers working across context, auth, execution, and reliability to build the action layer for AI agents.

We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed, with angel investors including Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of HubSpot), and Gokul Rajaram. Our customers range from YC startups to companies like Brex, Glean, Zoom, and more.


ABOUT THE TEAM

This is an applied AI engineering role, not a traditional support role. You will work directly with customers, learn the repeated work behind their problems, and build agentic systems that take that work over. When a customer needs direct engineering, you will debug and ship. When a pattern repeats, you will turn it into a workflow, eval, tool, or product capability that compounds.

•  The frontier: support is one of the richest applied AI environments — an agent has to gather context, reason across systems, use tools, take bounded action, verify the outcome, and communicate clearly. You design that system.

•  The trust bar: AI cannot be trusted by default with customer support. You define state, permissions, guardrails, evals, and escalation paths so the automation earns trust.

•  The feedback loop: it's immediate. Deploy into real support work, watch where the system fails, and improve it until people can hand over more of the job.

ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES


What you'll build

•  Agentic workflows that take over support functions: intake, classification, context gathering, reproduction, diagnosis, response drafting, remediation, verification, and follow-up.

•  Tool-using agents that safely inspect runs, logs, auth state, configuration, and provider behavior, then propose or execute bounded recovery actions.

•  Eval suites for diagnostic correctness, resolution quality, safe escalation, customer communication, and end-to-end task completion.

•  Human-in-the-loop systems that make ownership, uncertainty, approvals, handoffs, and failure states explicit.

•  The observability, memory, and feedback loops that let these agents improve from real support cases without repeating mistakes.

•  Product improvements that remove entire classes of customer issues instead of handling the same symptoms faster.


How you'll work

•  Start with the customer outcome, then work backward into the model, workflow, tooling, or product change required to deliver it.

•  Own the hardest issues end to end when direct engineering is needed: reproduce, isolate, mitigate, ship, communicate, and verify the resolution with the customer.

•  Sit with customers and partner with Support, FDE, Product, and Engineering to find work that should become software.

•  Move from a rough prototype to a reliable production workflow, with traces, evals, guardrails, and a clear human fallback.

•  Use frontier models, coding agents, and internal AI tools every day to multiply your own engineering output.

•  Measure success in customer outcomes improved, support work removed, and classes of failure prevented.


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

•  Experience level: 2–4 years of professional software engineering experience.

Applied AI engineering

•  You have built production systems with language models, tool calling, retrieval, structured outputs, multi-step workflows, or agent memory.

•  You know how to use models and coding agents as leverage, and where their non-determinism creates hidden risk.

•  You use evals, traces, failure analysis, and fast iteration to make AI systems dependable.

Strong systems engineering

•  You are an experienced backend, platform, or integration engineer who has shipped and operated production software.

•  You can debug across SDKs, HTTP, OAuth, webhooks, queues, data stores, logs, and third-party APIs.

•  You turn an ambiguous failure into a minimal reproduction, a root cause, and a durable fix.

Customer-adjacent building
 •  You are deliberately choosing to work closer to customers because you want a tighter loop between what you build and the impact it creates.

•  You enjoy talking directly with technical users, turning a vague problem into a system, and watching that system change their outcome.

•  You communicate clearly under uncertainty, ask the exact next question, and never bluff.


Workflow and product judgment
• You can model a support function as states, tools, permissions, handoffs, verification steps, and escalation rules.

•  You know what should be automated, what should remain human, and how to increase autonomy without reducing trust.

•  You fix the class of problem, not only the visible symptom.

OPTIONAL

•  TypeScript or Python in production.

•  Experience building AI agents, copilots, workflow automation, or eval infrastructure.

•  Experience with a developer platform, API product, support engineering, SRE, or incident response.

•  Familiarity with OAuth 2.0, webhooks, rate limits, Postgres, queues, and cloud observability.

•  Experience with support systems such as Plain, Zendesk, Intercom, or Salesforce.

•  Public technical writing, open source contributions, or unusually good debugging notes.

description:
At Composio, we are building infrastructure that allows agents to communicate with the tools you use for work including Github, Gmail, Notion, Salesforce, etc. We are a lean team of engineers wrangling problems from context to search, that help us provide the most capable bridge between your agents and your tools.

 

We raised a $25M Series A from Lightspeed https://lsvp.com/stories/investing-in-composio-building-the-backbone-of-ai-agent-intelligence/ with some incredible angels like Guillermo Rauch (CEO of Vercel), Dharmesh Shah (CTO of Hubspot), Gokul Rajaram. Beginning of this year we 3x our ARR with customers like Google, AWS, Mercor, Mintlify, Glean and Emergent.



running stateful agent infrastructure inside someone else's cluster is new territory. as our FDE intern, you'll help define what reliable, repeatable on-prem agent deployment looks like across customers running us in their own environments.




WHAT YOU'LL DO?

 - get hands-on with the on-prem lifecycle: helm charts, upgrades, the weekly release train, rollback paths.

 - help pull diverged customer forks back onto one supported chart, with guardrails.

 - contribute to onboarding so a new customer deploys in days, not weeks.

 - debug across the stack: temporal workflows, k8s init ordering, storage, auth-refresh pipelines.

 - support the security surface: CVE triage, patching, RCAs.


"MUST HAVES"

if you are very good, nothing is a must per-se

 - you've built in environments you don't fully control — homelab, VPC, self-hosted — and like figuring out why systems break.

 - curious about kubernetes and helm; you want to go deep.

 - ai native — you've built with language models and have opinions on agents and MCP

 - comfortable in linux; you can write a clear RCA.

 - human — you build trust and admit what you don't know.

BONUS: temporal, Postgres, cloud secret managers, self-hosted delivery (kots/airgap), open source or hackathon wins.

title: Engineering Support Lead
description:
ENGINEERING SUPPORT LEAD

Location: San Francisco · Full time


ABOUT COMPOSIO

Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. Our systems must be reliable at scale - agents must act correctly, integrations must be robust, and integration needs to be an autonomous, observable function that accelerates engineering rather than slowing it.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are hiring an Engineering Support Lead who is already doing technical support work and is ready to build the function for the AI era. You know the reality of a live queue, difficult escalations, customer communication, and coaching support engineers. Now you want to build the team, standards, and systems that make great support repeatable as Composio grows.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will stay close to customers and cases while hiring and developing the team, running support across locations, and using AI to help people resolve more problems well.


THE FRONTIER YOU'LL WORK ON

 - AI can gather context, suggest a diagnosis, and draft a reply. A strong support leader knows how to bring those capabilities into a real queue, check their quality, and keep a person accountable for the customer's outcome. You will shape that system.

 - Every difficult case is product signal. You will turn recurring failures across auth, SDKs, integrations, and agent workflows into fixes, clearer docs, better tools, and fewer future tickets.

 - Support must scale across time zones without losing ownership. You will build the coverage, handoffs, coaching, and escalation paths that make the experience consistent for customers and sustainable for the team.


WHAT WILL YOU DO?

 - Own the support queue end to end: triage, technical investigation, customer updates, escalation, and confirmation of resolution.

 - Lead complex enterprise cases. Reproduce failures across APIs, OAuth, SDKs, third-party integrations, and agent workflows; give Engineering a clear diagnosis and stay accountable while a fix ships.

 - Build the operating model across San Francisco and Bangalore, including queue ownership, shift handoffs, incident communication, and coverage that matches our commitments.

 - Set useful response and follow-up targets by customer tier and severity. Review case quality, unresolved work, customer outcomes, and the reasons customers contact us again.

 - Hire, onboard, and coach technical support engineers. Run case reviews, give direct feedback, and create paths for people to grow in support and engineering-adjacent work.

 - Bring AI into the daily support workflow. Use Composio and work with our applied AI engineers to improve intake, context gathering, investigation, drafting, and follow-up; measure quality and keep clear human ownership when a workflow fails.

 - Build a demand and capacity view that informs staffing and coverage decisions before the queue falls behind.

 - Work with FDE, Product, and Engineering to turn patterns in customer cases into product fixes, self-serve guidance, and better developer experience.


WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

We are looking for someone whose career is already rooted in technical support and who can show evidence of the following:

 - Operate support today. You currently lead or play a senior role in a technical support function. You have owned live cases, escalations, queue health, and the quality of customer communication.

 - Build a support organization. You have hired or coached support engineers, improved how a team works, set clear ownership and service standards, and can show how customer outcomes changed.

 - Go deep technically. You can inspect requests and logs, reproduce an ambiguous failure, reason about APIs and authentication, and work effectively with engineers on a durable fix.

 - Earn customer trust. You write clearly under uncertainty, give useful next steps, and stay with a customer through resolution rather than treating an internal handoff as closure.

 - Lead people and operations. You can design coverage across locations, run an escalation calmly, and make staffing decisions using evidence rather than ticket counts alone.

 - Be ready for AI-led support. You use AI tools in your own work and can identify where they will make support better, how to check their output, and when a person must take over. You are eager to build this into the team's daily practice.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience with a developer platform, API product, cloud infrastructure, or an integration-heavy product.

 - Experience building support automation, agent workflows, evaluations, or human review systems.

 - Experience reading or shipping Python or TypeScript fixes while working in support.

 - Familiarity with OAuth, webhooks, rate limits, MCP, and support tools such as Plain, Zendesk, or Intercom.

 - Experience building a team that spans the US and India.

Prior experience supporting an AI product is useful. What matters most is proven ownership in support and the drive to build a better support organization with AI.

title: APM - integrations
description:
WHO ARE WE?

Composio builds the AI-native automation layer for software teams: SDKs, runtimes, and platform tooling that let developers compose, evaluate, and operate agentic workflows and AI-powered products. Our systems must be reliable at scale - agents must act correctly, integrations must be robust, and integration needs to be an autonomous, observable function that accelerates engineering rather than slowing it. You'll join a small, high-leverage team building the delivery systems and metrics that give product and support teams visibility and predictable delivery.

This role is based in Bangalore (HSR).



WHO IS OUR IDEAL CANDIDATE?

A high-agency operator who is also AI-native, and who wants to grow into product. The role starts ops-heavy: you run the operations that get apps live on Composio, keep the toolkits healthy, and automate as much of that work as you can. Over 6-8 months, once those workflows and automations are running, the role shifts towards owning ambiguous product problems across the platform - triggers, tools, skills, auth, governance, and toolkit-level issues like rate limits and MCP hosting. This is not a traditional PM role with an engineering team to direct. It's closer to founder-mode ownership of a product line, where you solve problems using agents and a small ops team.

You've shipped things on your own - a side project, a tool, a micro-business, or a system you built that is still running - and you've run real operations with quality bars, not just executed inside someone else's process. You're at the edge of AI out of genuine curiosity: you use AI tools daily and can point to specific things you built or automated with them in the last month. You pick work by impact, not by how interesting it is, and you have no ego about manual work that isn't automated yet. You can hold a technical conversation with engineers without a translator, and you're comfortable owning problems that don't have a clear owner yet.



WHAT WILL THEY OWN?

 - The toolkit number: how many apps are live on Composio, and the health of the ones already live.

 - New apps, end to end: run the operations of getting them live - research, setup, QA, launch.

 - Existing toolkits: make them better with the product team, and clear the issues that stop them from working well.

 - QA and support for every toolkit you bring live. Once it's live, its quality is your problem.

 - The ops playbook: build it, run it, scale it. SOPs, small tools, AI agents before humans - you automate yourself first, and when scaling takes people, hiring them is part of the job.

 - The metrics for this function: define them, build them, watch them.

 - Product problems, as the ops layer starts running on its own: ambiguous, non-engineering problems across triggers, tools, auth, governance and toolkit-level issues - scoped, owned and shipped by you.
   


WHAT ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

 - Experience: 2-4 years. We care more about how fast you've grown than how senior you are.

 - Technical floor: can explain what an API and an integration are, reads API docs cold, writes enough code to build small tools and automations. Not an engineer; infra-level work is not the job.

 - AI-native automation instinct: your default answer to repeated work is "how do I never do this manually again" - backed by recent, specific evidence of things you've built or automated with AI.

 - Dirty-work appetite: you happily run the manual version today while the automation is being built. This and the automation instinct are both required; we never average them.

 - Process maturity: you've designed or owned a pipeline with throughput, SLAs, or quality bars, and you left systems running behind you - not just stories.

 - Product instinct: you can take a vague problem, figure out what's actually broken, and decide what to build or fix - without waiting for a spec or a dedicated engineering team.

 - Organized ownership: routines, follow-ups, nothing dropped. You communicate clearly, in writing and in person.

 - High agency in uncertainty: given a goal with no playbook and no owner above you, you define the problem yourself and start before permission.

 - Operating maturity: this role carries a number from week one, so it needs someone who has owned outcomes before. It is not internship-shaped.

We'll pass at any stage on candidates who only want the cool parts of the job, choose work by interestingness over impact, can't explain what an API is, or do the same manual work in month three as month one.



NICE-TO-HAVE

 - Founder or early-stage experience: you've taken something from zero, or joined early and owned a function.

 - Experience with SaaS integrations, API products, or developer-facing products.

 - Built things with agents or LLM workflows beyond personal use - tools, experiment logs, side projects other people use.

 - An engineering-adjacent path: studied engineering and moved into non-technical work, or a non-CS background with things you built on the side.

 - High-throughput ops backgrounds (delivery, marketplace, physical ops) count only alongside the AI-native bar above - on their own they are not this job.
   


OUTCOMES WE EXPECT IN THE FIRST 90 DAYS

 - More toolkits live on Composio - you own the supply number, and it moved.

 - Existing toolkits repaired or unblocked without anything breaking technically.

 - A v1 ops playbook running: SOPs, automations, and AI agents handling the repeatable parts of onboarding and QA.

 - Metrics for the function defined and visible: supply, health of supply, pipeline status.

 - What this is not: usage. Usage is a product metric; this role is measured on supply and the health of supply.
